_help: Questions for the Bedford history quiz. Each question: question text, a list of choices, answer = the NUMBER of the correct choice counting from 0 (first choice = 0, second = 1, ...), and a short explanation shown after answering. Visitors get up to 10 random questions per round. Keep verified = false until the Historical Society has checked it. ALL QUESTIONS BELOW ARE DRAFTS.

questions.question: In what year was Bedford incorporated as a town?
questions.explanation: Bedford was incorporated on September 23, 1729, which is why 2029 marks its 300th anniversary.

questions.question: Bedford was formed from parts of which two towns?
questions.explanation: Bedford was carved out of parts of Concord and Billerica.

questions.question: Where is the historic Bedford Flag preserved today?
questions.explanation: The Bedford Flag is preserved at the Bedford Free Public Library.

questions.question: Where did Bedford's Minutemen gather on the morning of April 19, 1775?
questions.explanation: Bedford's Minutemen gathered at Fitch Tavern before marching to Concord.

questions.question: Which Bedford captain was killed on April 19, 1775?
questions.explanation: Captain Jonathan Wilson of Bedford was killed during the fighting on April 19, 1775.

questions.question: Two Brothers Rocks are linked to which two colonial leaders?
questions.explanation: The rocks are said to mark the boundary between the lands of Governor John Winthrop and Thomas Dudley.

questions.question: Which river forms part of Bedford's western boundary?
questions.explanation: The Concord River runs along Bedford's western edge.

questions.question: Hanscom Field is named after whom?
questions.explanation: The airfield was named for Laurence G. Hanscom, a pilot and journalist.

questions.question: The Bedford VA hospital is named for which person?
questions.explanation: It is the Edith Nourse Rogers Memorial Veterans Hospital, named for the Massachusetts congresswoman.

questions.question: Which popular bike trail ends in Bedford?
questions.explanation: The Minuteman Bikeway runs from Cambridge to its end at Bedford Depot.

questions.question: What kind of museum is the Job Lane House?
questions.explanation: The Job Lane House is a historic farmhouse from the early 1700s, preserved as a museum.
